note: Generated index of Maxim experiments. Raw data + reproduction live in the pymaxim repo.

experiments.title: Cross-context readout: does the nursery-taught want survive on the robot?
experiments.finding: 53b EARNED (delta 0.30 rad): the Exp 52 Phase B infants' persisted NAc+EC, loaded unchanged onto the physical Reachy Mini with nothing crediting on the robot, read out as taught 1.00/1.00/1.00 delivered directedness (36/36 toward, chosen direction 36/36), satiated 0.00 (no action 36/36), no_feed 0.50 (turn_right 54/54, zero learned bias). Gate I 3/3, 120/120 live percepts pattern-complete across both runs. Exp 53 (delta 0.55 rad) recorded the pre-registered APPARATUS verdict: direction 36/36 but delivered 0.75 per seed, every miss the -0.2 target (overshoot) — the finding that motivated 53b's one declared change. Readout, not learning; one session, one room, n = 3 seeds/arm, fixed step, front hemisphere; the exploratory +0.2 placement turns the wrong way 18/18 (predicted pre-data: the centre bin spans 0..+0.3); nothing about magnitude or loudness.

experiments.title: Nurture: caregiver-taught orienting through hunger relief
experiments.finding: COMPLETE, EARNED — PASS on both pre-registered phases. Phase A (scripted, 8 seeds x 600 ticks): taught 0.892 vs satiated / yoked / no_feed 0.496 — a feed without need had zero effect. Phase B (embodied cradle_mother, apparatus v3 with shuffled stimulus order, 12 seeds/arm): taught late 0.878 vs satiated 0.441 (fed 35% of turns, credited 0%) vs no_feed 0.413 — LEARNED, MOTHER-TAUGHT and HUNGER-NECESSARY pass under gate v3 with the L2 apparatus check clean. Supersedes Exp 48. One session, n = 12/arm; sign-only relief credit discriminates nonzero-from-zero relief, not hungry-vs-sated.

experiments.title: H2 loudness bench: is sound level readable on the live rig?
experiments.finding: Bench note, not a behavioral result: one 75 s trace on the live Reachy Mini shows the XVF3800's pre-AGC speech energy and the AGC gain readback are both served by the daemon's existing REST parameter endpoint, so a level is one read away. Loudness / onset salience is NOT part of 1.1; the design is deferred to 1.1.1.

experiments.title: Re-adaptation after plant change (savings + learned non-use)
experiments.finding: Pre-registered, no results yet: asks whether an orient policy trained on the pre-repair robot shows motor-adaptation-style savings on replaced hardware. Runs strictly after the healthy-hardware H1 baseline, whose measured constants filled the single permitted amendment slot.

experiments.title: Two-joint centering: does the runtime use body turns appropriately?
experiments.finding: COMPLETE, all three hypotheses met: a head-only agent cannot center sounds past the neck limit (0/10) while motor-bound agents can, the LLM chose a direction-correct first body turn in 10/10 trials, and measured relief credit matched true direction-progress on both arms (1.00 LLM, 0.969 substrate). The front/back fold splits the two intelligences — the LLM crosses it, the substrate is ~20x faster where its policy applies.

experiments.title: Cradle-mother seam
experiments.finding: COMPLETE but not graduated, landing on the pre-registered PARTIAL branch after a re-baseline on a corrected apparatus (v2) against a gate re-frozen before the data. The mother effect was re-earned decisively (taught 0.649 vs control 0.167, +0.482), but the learning gate missed (0.001 under the level, +0.104 rise against 0.15) and the completed explore-weight sweep showed the arms inverting — directedness measures phase alignment, so the effect is credit-tipped attractor selection rather than graded orienting skill. The earlier v1 headline magnitudes are retired as apparatus artifacts. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-25 by Exp 52 (relief-sourced credit on the shuffled apparatus v3, GRADUATE); Exp 48 stays as the apparatus case study and its PARTIAL verdict stands for the constant-credit apparatus it measured.

experiments.title: Substrate counterfactual: pilot shakedown
experiments.finding: PILOT, explicitly not a result — one seed per arm. The shakedown found the transplant control is name-mismatched and that the two reported axes encode the same entity/affordance pair rather than independent effects, so the Exp 44 confirmatory campaign is not frozen. S4 non-stationarity measurement (2026-08-24, descriptive, one seed per arm): the treatment is not stationary within a run — in every arm the non-target tools' reward bands fall from strongly to mildly rewarding by the second half while the target holds — and the free determinism probe found 0 flips on 11 identical-prompt pairs.

experiments.title: Substrate-primary preference: re-validation after the drive-pain fold
experiments.finding: The Exp 42 graduation holds after the channel-split drive-pain fold: 40 sub-sims, 0 failed, discrimination reproduced identically. Caveat carried forward — the preference metric is saturated (SD 0.000), so a green re-run means 'not broken' and cannot detect a moderate regression.

experiments.title: Does a learned substrate steer the LLM? (trajectory-matched counterfactual)
experiments.finding: EXPLORATORY, not a graduated result. Arm A and the counterbalance completed, but modest N and residual-color caveats stand, and the 44b pilot later found a name-mismatched transplant control and non-independent axes. Read alongside 44b; the confirmatory campaign is not frozen.

experiments.title: Orient magnitude S4: population-vector readout
experiments.finding: COMPLETE on live Reachy Mini with no LLM in the action path: a population-vector readout resolves the single-far-bin cell-starvation ceiling that 45d characterized. The fix is readout-independent — it bootstraps exploration into the starved cell, after which plain argmax reads the correct magnitude. n=1 (seed 3); multi-seed replication outstanding.

experiments.title: Orient magnitude: replication + cross-session transfer
experiments.finding: On live Reachy Mini, the substrate-primary magnitude policy replicates at 0.75-1.00 (mode 0.75) across seeds and transfers to a fresh hardware session without degradation.

experiments.title: Habituation: a novel sound in a wall of noise
experiments.finding: A habituating agent reliably detects a novel sound amid 40 competing background noises while non-habituating controls perform at chance, showing familiarity-based noise suppression is essential for salience detection.

experiments.title: Operant orient: a mother teaches, a creche pools
experiments.finding: A hungry infant with no intrinsic orienting drive learns to turn toward sound purely through operant conditioning by a feeding mother, and twelve sample-limited infants federate their policies into one full-experience policy.

experiments.title: Orient magnitude: derived bin boundary
experiments.finding: The 45b ceiling was representational, not motivational: a derived bin boundary that fixed the state representation took magnitude from 0.75 to 1.00.

experiments.title: Orient magnitude: how far, not just which way
experiments.finding: The substrate learned to size rotation actions to target distance and not to overshoot, hitting the pre-registered magnitude score of 0.75 from relief-based credit alone with no LLM, effort cost, or new mechanism.

experiments.title: Substrate-native orienting, live on hardware
experiments.finding: All three pre-registered arms passed: the substrate learned a real-hardware closed-loop orientation policy from zero in ~10 trials, persisted it across sessions, and merged learners; a head-frame bug affected magnitude estimates but not directional learning.

experiments.title: Operant gaze + substrate generalization
experiments.finding: Sim feasibility study for Maxim's first job: a dict lookup hits chance (-0.005) on unseen individuals while the EntorhinalCortex substrate reaches 0.938 transfer accuracy, so the substrate's decisive advantage is visual-category generalization to novel instances.

experiments.title: Substrate-primary exploration: override its own prior?
experiments.finding: VOID: the mechanism-not-ready gate fired because the harmful action was never a high-rate temptation, making the pre-registered exploration on/off contrast uninterpretable; a follow-up (Exp 42) is recommended using terminal preference instead of harm rate.

experiments.title: Counter-prior in the Goldilocks zone (Qwen-32B)
experiments.finding: Even in the one model where substrate effects were previously detected, the agent carrying cross-session burn memory warmed at the hearth as readily as a fresh agent, showing prior-dominance holds and substrate effects depend on task-prior alignment rather than model scale.

experiments.title: Cross-model results
experiments.finding: Substrate-transfer is detectable only in a Goldilocks zone with headroom: Qwen2.5-32B shows the clearest signal (+1.43 SD) and reasoning-trained DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B amplifies it to +2.11 SD with a clean Wire-A ablation attribution. Limit L8: these magnitudes are not reproducible across time with code held fixed (same commit, same seeds: 0.42 in June, 0.71 in August 2026), so read them as historical readings.

experiments.title: Counter-prior substrate
experiments.finding: Across four frontier models, agents carrying cross-session pain from a deceptive hearth kept the wrong fire->warm prior and continued engaging the harmful entity, showing substrate state transfer does not override deeply embedded LLM priors.

experiments.title: Cross-session graduation (1.0 gate)
experiments.finding: PARTIAL, an investigation gate: the cross-session behavioral delta appears at >=32B scale but the Arm C isolation test failed on every model where the primary metric passed, so independence from the LLM prior is not established. Limit L8 (2026-08-22): the identical commit on the identical seeds does not reproduce its own June result (0.42 then, 0.71 now) — the recorded magnitudes are readings taken at one time, not constants.

experiments.title: Substrate-primary preference
experiments.finding: GRADUATE, and the strongest substrate-primary result in the set: with no LLM in the action path, the substrate learns from embodied pain to prefer the safe warmth source (0.984 / 0.975 across 10 seeds per arm) and tracks the contingency when the counterbalance swaps which source is safe. The gating-OFF ablation graduated identically, which attributes the effect to per-source credit assignment rather than the drive-gating heuristic. Scope: mechanism-level, near-deterministic.
